subject: Buyer decision latency & split-term structuring for AWS Private Offer (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 4 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Buyer decision latency & split-term structuring for AWS Private Offer (Acme Corp)

Team — quick recap from this morning's call with Acme procurement and engineering. Key points:

- Procurement (Susan Lee) says finance will only sign a 12‑month commercial commitment, but the engineering org wants a 6‑month pilot window before rolling to enterprise.
- They prefer a single purchase flow if possible (marketplace private offer) but with activation/entitlement gating: pilot resources for 6 months, then automatic conversion or full activation after legal/CFO signoff.
- Decision latency: procurement needs invoices to align with AWS Marketplace billing; final signoff timeline is ~10 business days for pilot acceptance.

Asks:
1) What's the simplest private‑offer structure we can present that meets both constraints (single PO + staged activation)?
2) What buyer approval gates do we need to anticipate on the AWS Marketplace side (procurement, BU legal, CFO, technical approver)?
3) Can we model split pricing (pilot discounted rate + conversion at renewal) and enumerate implications for activation/entitlements?

I've attached a quick scenario matrix (acme_po_scenario_matrix.xlsx) with proposed banding — please review and flag any operational blockers. I want to send a first draft to Susan by COB Monday.

Thanks,

Sofia Ivanova
Head of BD, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_po_scenario_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Buyer decision latency & split-term structuring for AWS Private Offer (Acme Corp)

+1 on the single‑PO with staged activation approach — operationally this is cleaner for procurement and reduces billing fragmentation. Two quick notes:

- Approval banding: we'll need Procurement (Susan), BU Legal (contracts review), and CFO signoff. On AWS Marketplace, buyer must accept private offer and then we can control entitlements server‑side. If CFO wants a 12‑month commercial commitment, we can structure the contract term as 12 months with a 6‑month "pilot bundle" priced at a discount, which auto‑bills into the 12‑month commitment after conversion.
- Activation gating: suggest we use a staged entitlements plan: Tier 1 (pilot) enabled upon acceptance, Tier 2 (full) enabled after DocuSign or CFO approval. This avoids two separate POs.

I'll loop in SE for technical entitlements and billing mapping. Jordan — can you run a quick check on how Redwood Private/Dedicated activations map to marketplace entitlements? Vivek — any concerns from co‑sell or marketplace activation windows?

Vanessa

Attachments: proposed_private_offer_terms.pdf (pdf)
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procure@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Buyer decision latency & split-term structuring for AWS Private Offer (Acme Corp)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the summary and the matrix. A few clarifications from our side:

- We cannot issue two separate POs for the same program; procurement prefers a single PO with clear milestone gating tied to entitlements and billing. So the single‑PO + staged activation approach sounds acceptable.
- CFO approval flow: CFO signs only after our legal signs off. Legal needs to see the private offer terms and a clear conversion price after the pilot.
- Timeline: we aim to decide on the pilot within 10 business days. Can you provide a version of the private offer that shows pilot pricing, conversion pricing, and the entitlement gating mechanics? Also include sample invoice language for AWS Marketplace.

Links: https://acme.sharepoint.com/sites/CloudPurchasing/Forms/AllItems.aspx

Best,
Susan
Purchasing Manager, Acme Corporation

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Buyer decision latency & split-term structuring for AWS Private Offer (Acme Corp)

Thanks Susan — good clarity. Next steps on our side:

- Vanessa & Jordan: draft private offer terms (single PO, 12‑month legal term, 6‑month pilot pricing with defined conversion price) and include sample Marketplace invoice language. Attach to HubSpot and share DocuSign link.
- Vivek: confirm co‑sell eligibility and whether any Marketplace enablement approvals will delay the timeline.
- Laura: prepare a short activation runbook for entitlements — how we flip Tier 1 -> Tier 2 and the signals (DocuSign completed / CFO sign) we use.

I'll target a draft to Susan by EOD Monday (2026‑07‑06). Adding HubSpot/DocuSign links here for reference:

Sofia
